topics.name: Angles in a triangle (school question bank)

questions.q: Which geometric term best describes {x}?
pairs: a beam of light from a laser pointer
a straight highway that goes on forever in both directions
a single star in the night sky
a torch beam shining into the sky
the tip of a sharp needle
a railway track imagined to go on endlessly both ways
questions.e: {x} → {ans}. Point: a location. Segment: two end points. Ray: one start point. Line: no end points.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a line segment and a line?
questions.a: A segment has two end points and a fixed length; a line has no end points
w: A line has two end points; a segment has none
A segment goes on forever in one direction
questions.e: A line extends endlessly in both directions, so it cannot be measured.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A ray has two end points.
Reason (R): A ray starts from one point and extends endlessly in one direction.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
w: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
questions.e: A ray has only ONE end point, so A is false; R correctly describes a ray.

questions.q: A robot arm starts flat on the table (0°) and turns {x} of a full circle. What angle does it make?
questions.e: A full turn is 360°, so {x} of it is {ans}.

questions.q: A robot arm starts flat on the table (0°) and turns {x} of a full circle. What angle does it make?
questions.e: A full turn is 360°, so {x} of it is {ans}.

questions.q: A {x} turn makes which type of angle?
questions.e: ¼ turn = 90°, ½ turn = 180°, ¾ turn = 270°, ⅛ turn = 45°, ⅓ turn = 120°.

questions.q: A {x} turn makes which type of angle?
questions.e: ¼ turn = 90°, ½ turn = 180°, ¾ turn = 270°, ⅛ turn = 45°, ⅓ turn = 120°.

questions.q: Fatima opens her scissors slightly to cut thread. Mariam opens hers wide to cut cardboard. Who makes the larger angle?
questions.a: Mariam – her blades are turned further apart
w: Fatima – smaller openings make bigger angles
Both are equal because the scissors are the same
It depends on how long the blades are
questions.e: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between the arms, not the length of the arms.

questions.q: At {x}, the hands of a clock make which type of angle?
questions.e: Hour marks are 30° apart: count the gaps between the hands (take the smaller angle). {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: At {x}, the hands of a clock make which type of angle?
questions.e: Hour marks are 30° apart: count the gaps between the hands (take the smaller angle). {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: At {x}, the hands of a clock make which type of angle?
questions.e: Hour marks are 30° apart: count the gaps between the hands (take the smaller angle). {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: At {h}:00, what is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
questions.e: Each hour gap is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°, so {h} gaps = {ans}°.

questions.q: At 1:30, what is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock?
questions.e: The minute hand is at 6 (180° from 12). The hour hand is halfway between 1 and 2 (45° from 12). 180° − 45° = 135°. (Careful: it is not 45°.)

questions.q: A skate ramp must meet the ground at an angle less than 90°. Which could be the ramp’s angle?
questions.e: Less than 90° means an acute angle, so {ans}° works.

questions.q: A laptop screen makes an angle of {s}° with the keyboard. You push the screen forward (closing it) by {c}°. What is the new angle?
questions.e: Closing makes the angle smaller: {s}° − {c}° = {ans}°. Check its type: under 90° is acute, over 90° is obtuse.

questions.q: A laptop screen is open at {s}°. You open it further by {c}°. What is the new angle?
questions.e: Opening makes the angle larger: {s}° + {c}° = {ans}° (an obtuse angle).

questions.q: Which is greater: a right angle or a straight angle?
questions.a: A straight angle (180°) – twice a right angle
questions.e: Right angle = 90°, straight angle = 180°.

questions.q: What are the arms of ∠OBQ?
questions.e: The middle letter is the vertex (B); the arms start at B and pass through O and Q.

questions.q: What are the arms of ∠PQR?
questions.e: The middle letter Q is the vertex; the arms are QP and QR.

questions.q: Why do perpendicular lines always form right angles?
questions.a: Perpendicular lines are defined as lines that meet at 90°
w: Because they are the same length
questions.e: If two lines meet at 90°, all four angles formed are right angles.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Every obtuse angle is greater than a right angle.
Reason (R): A right angle measures 90°.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.e: An obtuse angle lies between 90° and 180°, so it is always greater than 90°.

questions.q: When drawing ∠A = 55° with a protractor, where must the vertex A be placed?
questions.a: On the centre point of the protractor, with one arm along the 0° line
w: At the end of the scale
questions.e: Centre on the vertex, base arm on 0°, then mark 55° on the scale that starts from 0.

questions.q: The arm of an angle points to 60 on the outer scale and 120 on the inner scale. The base arm lies along the 0° of the outer scale. What is the angle?
questions.e: Always read the scale that starts at 0 on the base arm – here the outer scale gives 60°.

questions.q: To draw an obtuse angle of 135°, the arm must be drawn…
questions.a: past the 90° mark, at 135 on the scale that starts from 0
w: on the 45° mark of the same scale
questions.e: Obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°; 135° = 90° + 45°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the three angles inside any triangle?
questions.e: The angles of every triangle add up to a straight angle, 180°.

questions.q: Two angles of a triangle are {a}° and {b}°. Find the third angle.
One angle of a triangle is 90° and another is {b}°. Find the third angle.
questions.e: 180° − 90° − {b}° = {ans}°. The other two angles of a right triangle add up to 90°.
